title: Thought, act, observe — on a 7B
spec: M12 · a ReAct loop that exits on stop, and the question that needs no tool at all
intro: Two turns of visible reasoning, a second search shaped by the first result, and an exit through finish_reason rather than the safety cap. Then the harder test: a question that should produce no tool call at all.
foot: Run it for real: labs-opensource/M12-react-agent-loop/ — python solution/react_agent.py, then labs-opensource/M05-function-calling/ for the no-tool case

steps.title: Turn 1 — the thought comes before the call
narrative: ReAct is three moves in a loop: reason about what you know and what is missing, act by calling a tool, observe the result. The reasoning is not decoration — it is what makes the next tool call better than a guess, and it is what you read when the agent goes wrong.

On a hosted model you would get this for free. On Mistral-7B you have to demand it in the system prompt, in capitals: before EVERY tool call, write Thought: [your reasoning]. The thought then arrives as msg.content alongside the tool call, and the loop prints it before executing anything.
Turn 1 does exactly that: it states a two-part plan — landscape first, then the specific SDK — and issues the broad search.
steps.youDo: python solution/react_agent.py and watch for a Thought: line above every [tool call].

steps.title: Turn 2 — the second query comes from the first answer
narrative: This is the move that separates a ReAct loop from two searches in a row. Turn 2's thought explicitly references what turn 1 returned — I now have the framework landscape — and narrows to what is still missing, so the query becomes "claude agent sdk features" rather than another broad sweep.

Mechanically this works because the observation went back into messages as a tool-role entry. The model is not remembering; it is re-reading. Drop the observation from the history and the second query degenerates into a rephrasing of the first.
steps.claudeSays: It has the list of frameworks but not the comparison target's feature set, so it spends its second call on the half of the question it cannot yet answer.

steps.title: Turn 3 — it stops because it is finished
narrative: Turn 3 issues no tool call. finish_reason comes back as "stop", the loop returns msg.content, and the report prints with all three required sections: Summary, Key Findings, Sources Used.

The distinction that matters is which exit fired. max_turns=20 is a safety cap — a circuit breaker for a loop that has stopped making progress, not a completion signal. If your agent routinely exits at the cap, it is not finishing, it is being cut off, and the report you get is a partial result wearing a report's formatting.
Three turns is typical with the mock search backend. Turn count is not a pass criterion; exiting through stop is.

after.title: WHAT TO ASSERT IN A TEST

view.text: Pin the three things the lab pins: a Thought: line appears before every tool call, the loop exits via stop and not the cap, and the report contains all three sections. Do not pin the turn count or the query strings — a 7B will phrase "python ai frameworks 2025" six different ways across six runs and every one of them is correct.

steps.title: The test that passes by doing nothing
narrative: Give the same tool-equipped agent a question it does not need a tool for. From the M05 suite: "What's the capital of France?" The correct trace has no [tool call] line at all — finish_reason is "stop" on the very first pass and the answer comes straight back.

Every other case in that suite calls exactly one tool: get_weather for Tokyo, calculate for the arithmetic, get_time for London. The France case is there to check the opposite skill — knowing when not to reach for a tool. An agent that searches the web for the capital of France is burning a round trip on something already in its weights.

And here the track is candid where a hosted-model course would not be: Mistral-7B occasionally calls a tool anyway, or answers the arithmetic from memory instead of calling calculate. The lab's own advice is to re-run or sharpen the tool descriptions if routing seems off. Tool routing on a local 7B is a tendency, not a guarantee — so keep the tool set small, describe each one narrowly, and never let a correctness-critical path depend on the model choosing to call it.
